transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Winsor Johnston.
The Justice Department's scrutiny of television networks is adding to pressure on broadcasters from the Trump administration.
NPR's David Falkenflick says it comes as one company is challenging a sweeping review of their local station licenses.
ABC and its parent company, Disney, are suing the president's chief broadcast regulator,
who basically said he was going to have a review of all eight of their local TV licenses at the same time,
essentially a threat to their bottom line, effectively unprecedented.
Now Trump is doing that, too, with investigations, delegitimization, jumping from one action item to the next,
kind of going from an exercise of leverage of power to the aura of abuse of power.
That's NPR's David Falkenflick reporting.
Cleanup operations are underway across parts of the southeastern U.S.
after Hurricane Esai-Eas made landfall along the Florida panhandle Friday night.
At least four people were killed, and hundreds of thousands of customers are without power.
NPR's Debbie Elliott reports.
Milton, Florida is a quaint and leafy town northeast of Pensacola.
Now it's a big mess with trees uprooted and others snapped in two.
Fire Chief John E. Rebel says they're on houses, in yards and over roads.
What we're seeing is a result of wind, and it was shocking how strong the winds were in this area.
Shocking because Milton is nearly 50 miles northwest of where the hurricane made landfall.
Now the hum of generators is in the air, and chainsaw crews are clearing trees from the roads.
President Karen Milstead says they'll get through.
Clean up, go on.
That could take a while. Debbie Elliott, NPR News, Milton, Florida.
The Kremlin is providing new details about a phone call between President Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The discussions on Friday ended with Trump announcing the U.S. would lift sanctions on Russian diesel exports in an attempt to bring down global prices.
NPR's Charles Maines reports from Moscow.
According to a Kremlin aide, the two leaders spoke for an hour and a half with Trump warmly congratulating Putin over his recent 74th birthday and neither president eager to put down the phone.
The primary outcome of the call, a Kremlin promised to immediately deliver 300,000 tons of Russian diesel fuel to U.S. and global markets, with more to follow.
To do so, Russia lifted its own embargo on diesel exports and moved the Kremlin imposed this summer after Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian energy facilities caused fuel shortages.
Trump has since praised the deal as a Russian gesture aimed at helping curb high diesel prices while blaming Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries for stoking the problem.
Charles Maines, NPR News, Moscow.
This is NPR News.
Authorities have locked down large parts of New Delhi today to block a youth-led protest.
Demonstrators are demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner over changes to voter lists.
The government denies wrongdoing.
Demonstrations are continuing in New York City over a shooting involving ICE agents.
A 28-year-old Dominican national was shot on Thursday while driving in the Bronx with his 5-year-old son in the backseat.
Protestor Iliana Lando says agents put the child in danger.
I think it's completely inappropriate that he was shot at in his car with his 5-year-old child.
I am a teacher. I believe that we should protect all children no matter if their parents are criminals or not.
Just because you are a criminal does not mean that you deserve to die in front of your child.
The man's son was not injured.
It's pumpkin spice season and some shoppers are paying more for their fall-themed products.
Stephen Besaha reports.
There's an almost 9 percent pumpkin spice premium, up a bit from last year.
Matt Schultz is chief consumer finance analyst at Lending Tree, which did the research.
He says some of the spooky season bump could be because pumpkins are slightly more expensive this year, but also...
Retailers understand how much people love pumpkin spice and how they might be willing to pay a little bit extra for it.
Now, this does vary by store.
If you take the time to look around at different places, you might be able to save yourself a little money.
Out of the six retailers it looked at, Lending Tree says Starbucks and Trader Joe's had the biggest fall flavor hikes.
Thanks.
Steven Masaha, NPR News.
This is NPR.
